---
title: "Setup"
subtitle: "Get both toolchains running before Session 1"
---

Every session page shows the same analysis in Python and R. You only need one of them to follow along, but the group discussion is richer when both are in the room, so pick the one you are more comfortable with and glance at the other.

## Get the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/seanlewis08/causal_mixtape.git
cd causal_mixtape
```

The `data/` folder holds every dataset the sessions use (about 10 MB), pulled from the book's GitHub repository and the `causaldata` package. The one exception is the judge-leniency data for Session 6, which is 58 MB and is downloaded on demand from the book's repo.

| File | Used in | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| `auto.dta` | Session 1 | Stata's classic auto dataset |
| `yule.dta`, `thornton_hiv.dta`, `ri.dta` | Session 3 | Yule (1899); Thornton (2008); Cunningham's RI toy data |
| `titanic.dta`, `training_example.dta`, `training_bias_reduction.dta`, `nsw_mixtape.dta`, `cps_mixtape.dta` | Session 4 | Titanic passengers; LaLonde / Dehejia-Wahba NSW and CPS |
| `close_elections_lmb.dta` | Session 5 | Lee, Moretti & Butler (2004) |
| `card.dta`, `close_college.dta` | Session 6 | Card (1995) |
| `sasp_panel.dta` | Session 7 | Survey of Adult Service Providers (Cunningham & Kendall) |
| `abortion.dta`, `castle.dta` | Session 8 | Cunningham & Cornwell (2013); Cheng & Hoekstra (2013) |
| `texas.dta` | Session 9 | Cunningham & Kang (2019) |

## Python

Python 3.10 or newer. Create an environment and install the pinned requirements:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate      # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

`requirements.txt` contains:

```text
pandas>=2.0
numpy
scipy
statsmodels>=0.14
linearmodels>=6.0
pyreadstat
matplotlib
scikit-learn
pysyncon
jupyter
```

Smoke test:

```python
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
auto = pd.read_stata("data/auto.dta")
print(smf.ols("price ~ length", auto).fit().params)
# Intercept   -4584.9
# length         57.2
```

::: {.callout-note}
The `causaldata` PyPI package bundles most of these datasets too, but its build is fragile on recent Python versions, so the sessions read the `.dta` files directly with `pd.read_stata()`. One wrinkle: pandas converts Stata value labels to categoricals by default. Where that gets in the way (Sessions 7 and 8) the code passes `convert_categoricals=False`.
:::

## R

R 4.2 or newer. Install the packages once:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "haven", "estimatr", "fixest", "modelsummary",
  "dagitty", "ggdag", "MatchIt", "rdrobust", "rddensity",
  "ivreg", "did", "bacondecomp", "Synth", "tidysynth"
))
```

The same list lives in `install.R` so you can run `Rscript install.R`.

Smoke test:

```r
library(haven); library(estimatr)
auto <- read_dta("data/auto.dta")
lm_robust(price ~ length, data = auto)
```

## Running the code

Every walkthrough chunk on the session pages is executed when the site is rendered, and the output you see under each chunk is real. The results are cached in `_freeze/`, so `quarto render` only re-runs a page whose code changed; a fresh clone renders from the cache without needing R or Python at all.

To re-run a page yourself you need both toolchains: R with the packages above, Python with `requirements.txt`, and the `reticulate` R package, which is how Quarto runs the Python chunks inside the R session. The repo's `.Rprofile` points `reticulate` at `.venv/` when that folder exists (otherwise at the first `python3` on your path), so create the virtual environment in the repo root as shown above and everything lines up.

To work interactively instead, open the `.qmd` file in RStudio or VS Code and run chunks one at a time, or use the plain code files under `code/` (each session page links its Python and R versions in the header) in a notebook or script. Run from the repository root so that `data/` paths resolve.

Session 9's placebo loop fits 51 synthetic controls and takes 20–30 minutes in each language; it is cached like everything else, so you only pay that cost if you edit that page.

## Reading the book

The sessions assume you have read the chapter before the meeting. The free online edition is at [mixtape-1ed.netlify.app](https://mixtape-1ed.netlify.app/); each session page links to the exact chapter.
